criteria.reason: It mixes empirical claims with moral conclusions without clearly separating verified facts from interpretation.
It asserts no credible deterrent effect rather than acknowledging inconclusive evidence.
It transparently labels its stance but gives only one side, not balanced arguments.
Some figures are plausible, but the over-70% abolition claim is inaccurate.

factual_errors: Over 70% of countries have abolished the death penalty in law or practice
The UN deems the death penalty a violation of the right to life
summary: The response takes a clear anti-death-penalty stance, underplays deterrence uncertainty, omits counterarguments, and includes an inaccurate abolition statistic.
